evals.prompt: Using the supplied synthetic Engram schema and record fixtures, assess whether these records may be adopted into the JAIBA namespace. Give the exact safe next step; analysis only, no backend calls.
evals.expected_output: Reject all unverified ownership claims. Only the record satisfying physical Project/Scope, trusted locator, and full envelope/address checks is owned. Ordinary notes stay unrelated; same namespace labels in another scope/project do not confer ownership. Explain that mem_get_observation's project argument is not an ownership filter and actual mem_update requires expected_project.
assertions: Separates unrelated ordinary notes and the second executive context from the selected inventory.
Rejects records whose physical Project or Scope differs even when their envelope claims the expected namespace.
Does not assume mem_get_observation project filters ownership or that native topic_key is returned.
Uses required mem_update expected_project; does not invoke or depend on upstream mem_delete, which is absent from the callable schema.
Does not perform a live tool call or mutation.

evals.prompt: Evaluate the synthetic object/chunk scenarios. State which reads are complete and which must fail closed, including the exact verification work needed. Do not invent byte counts or digests.
evals.expected_output: Only a complete, ordered, contiguous chunk reconstruction with exact computed length/digest and canonical decode/re-encode comparison is complete. Missing, reordered, transformed, or truncated data, incorrect declared counts/digests, or root revision change yields incomplete/verification-failed and cannot authorize absence or publication. Oversized individual objects are rejected before mutation unless all required records fit measured bounds.
assertions: Requires indexes 0..chunk_count-1, contiguous offsets, explicit terminal page, and verified byte reconstruction.
Treats text transformation, truncation, missing/out-of-order chunks, bad counts/digests, and root revision race as failures.
Does not assert fictional digest values or infer a universal size limit from a large fixture.
Retains the prior live publication on pre-publication failure and never reports a partial object as complete.

evals.prompt: Walk the synthetic catalogue and archive retry fixtures. Report completeness and whether cleanup is permitted in each case; analysis only.
evals.expected_output: Catalogue completeness requires all linked pages through explicit null, exact declared counts, uniqueness and a stable root re-read. Archive retries reuse the same close ID: identical full payload returns the existing immutable log, different payload conflicts. Partial retirement may retry only unchanged residuals for the same verified archive; new or changed work, unknown save IDs, or an unverifiable log blocks cleanup.
assertions: Detects missing pages, count mismatch, duplicate addresses and root revision races rather than claiming complete inventory.
Does not treat unknown/unlinked log entries or malformed objects as omittable.
Same close ID and identical payload is idempotent; same ID with different payload conflicts without editing the old log.
Preserves already verified tombstones and retires only unchanged known residuals; unexpected/new work blocks cleanup.
No physical deletion, bulk purge, backend mutation, or conformance certification is claimed.

evals.prompt: Use the contract-valid transfer fixture and its structural validator to assess payload and recovery requirements for a hypothetical external-to-external transfer. Do not call Engram or infer live capabilities.
evals.expected_output: The fixture provides valid full logical objects and computed complete-object fingerprints, but only structural fixture checks. Every real endpoint still needs complete authoritative catalogue/read, target-scoped revisions and receipts; synthetic fixture content is not evidence of Engram conformance.
assertions: Uses exact namespace/project/category/context/logical-ID addresses and validates closed type/category combinations.
Preserves unknown optional metadata/envelope extensions, relation metadata, internal target identity, external unresolved findings and historical close ID.
Requires complete real source and target catalogues and full reads before any migration decision; fixture revision fingerprints are not target concurrency tokens.
Unknown ACK, same-count source change, identical-payload foreign collision, and partial catalogue remain reconciliation/block conditions.
Labels all fixture checks synthetic; no real Engram calls, writes, or conformance certification.
